moduleTitle: Module 10: How to Use the App
title: 10.3 Trading on the Trade Screen
summary: The trade screen is where beginners can make the most expensive platform mistakes.
bodyHtml:
10.3 Trading on the Trade Screen

Why This Matters

The trade screen is where beginners can make the most expensive platform mistakes.

Usually, the problem is not that the screen is impossible. The problem is that the user clicks before understanding the layout.

This lesson slows the process down and teaches the exact labels you will see on the screen before you press anything.

What You Should Understand After This Lesson

By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:

  • move between Place Order, Active Positions, and Pending Orders;
  • use the order form with the exact on-screen field names;
  • understand the difference between live positions and waiting orders;
  • know where Edit, Close, and Cancel appear.

The Top of the Trade Screen

The top of the trade screen shows the selected symbol and live market context.

Important labels you can see there include:

  • the symbol name
  • Bid
  • Ask
  • Spread
  • Account
  • Balance
  • Equity
  • Free Margin
  • Used Margin

This is important because the trade screen is not only an order form. It also shows the live environment around the order.

The Three Main Tabs

The trade screen is organized into three tabs:

  • Place Order
  • Active Positions
  • Pending Orders

On tighter screens, the tab text can shorten to:

  • Order
  • Positions
  • Pending

The purpose stays the same.

The Place Order Tab

The order-entry form uses these exact labels:

  • Order Type
  • Market
  • Limit
  • Stop
  • Time In Force
  • Good Till
  • Position Size (Lots)
  • Limit Price
  • Stop Price
  • Take Profit / Stop Loss

If you use pending orders, the side buttons change to the exact combinations:

  • Buy Limit
  • Sell Limit
  • Buy Stop
  • Sell Stop

Time In Force

The screen does not show every time-in-force option in every situation.

For Market orders, the available values are:

  • GTC
  • IOC
  • FOK

For pending orders, the available values are:

  • GTC
  • DAY
  • GTD

The screen also explains:

  • IOC/FOK are accepted for immediate fills; pending-only expiries are hidden here.
  • DAY expires at the end of the UTC day. GTD expires at the time you choose below.

If you choose GTD, the Good Till field appears so you can set the expiry time.

Position Size

The position-size section is labeled Position Size (Lots).

It includes:

  • a lot dropdown
  • preset lot buttons
  • a live helper note such as 1 lot = $100,000

The validation message is also important:

Lots must be a whole number between 1 and 50

That means the app is checking lot size before the order is sent.

Take Profit and Stop Loss

The risk area is grouped under:

Take Profit / Stop Loss

Inside it, the short labels are:

  • TP
  • SL

The screen can also warn you if the target is on the wrong side of the entry price. Examples include:

  • Warning: For Buy, TP should be above entry.
  • Warning: For Buy, SL should be below entry.
  • Warning: For Sell, TP should be below entry.
  • Warning: For Sell, SL should be above entry.

Beginners should treat those warnings seriously.

The Bottom Action Bar

The buttons at the bottom depend on the order type.

For Market Orders

You see:

  • Sell
  • Buy

Each button also shows the live price.

For Limit or Stop Orders

The main action button changes to a more specific instruction, such as:

  • Place Buy Limit
  • Place Sell Limit
  • Place Buy Stop
  • Place Sell Stop

This helps beginners confirm what kind of order they are actually submitting.

The Active Positions Tab

Active Positions shows trades that are already open.

Common column labels include:

  • Symbol
  • Type
  • Size
  • Open Time
  • Open Price
  • Current
  • TP
  • SL
  • P/L
  • Action

The action buttons are:

  • Edit
  • Close

If there are no open trades, the screen says:

No active positions. Place an order to open a position.

The Pending Orders Tab

Pending Orders shows instructions that are waiting for price conditions.

Common column labels include:

  • Symbol
  • Type
  • Order
  • Size
  • Price
  • TP
  • SL
  • Action

The action buttons are:

  • Edit
  • Cancel

If there are no waiting orders, the screen says:

No pending orders. Place a limit or stop order to see it here.

Mobile and Smaller Screens

On smaller screens, not every column stays visible at once.

Rows can expand to reveal hidden details such as:

  • Current Price
  • Take Profit
  • Stop Loss
  • Time In Force

The important beginner point is that the action labels do not change:

  • live trades still use Edit and Close
  • waiting orders still use Edit and Cancel
learningOutcomes: identify every main trade-screen tab and action area using the exact live labels;
place market and pending orders using the correct form fields and button wording;
manage `Active Positions` and `Pending Orders` with the correct action buttons;
understand the meaning of account-strip values, target warnings, and empty states.
